title: is_fips flag on provider struct is the authoritative FIPS boundary marker — not fips_gate presence
description: The registry uses p->is_fips on the struct crypto2dev_provider as the authoritative marker for FIPS boundary membership. The FIPS enforcement filter in crypto2dev_lookup_algo(), fips_aggregate(), and fips_provider_loaded() all check is_fips, not whether fips_gate is non-NULL. This is correct because these are orthogonal concepts: a non-FIPS provider could have a non-NULL fips_gate stub that always returns 0 (not-FIPS does not mean ungated), and a FIPS provider might have some algorithms without a per-algo gate (the module check may be provider-level, not per-algo). Using fips_gate \!= NULL as a proxy for 'is FIPS certified' would misclassify both cases. A reviewer might suggest 'simplify by checking fips_gate \!= NULL instead of a separate is_fips field' — that conflates operational gating with CMVP certification boundary membership, which are different properties.
close_reason: Correct design: is_fips flag on provider struct is the authoritative FIPS boundary marker. It is set at provider registration time by the provider itself (wolfssl sets is_fips=1). The flag cannot be spoofed by userspace — providers are kernel modules loaded by root. FIPS enforcement is provider-declared, not user-declared.
